title: Secret audio captures 'Crypto King' planning his own kidnapping, defence lawyer says
summary: So-called "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski sounded "cool and collected" in a secret audio recording taken by his alleged kidnappers, according to one of their defence lawyers, who suggested the…

blocks.text: Toronto·New

So-called "Crypto King" Aiden Pleterski sounded "cool and collected" in a secret audio recording taken by his alleged kidnappers, according to one of their defence lawyers, who suggested the recording was made as an "insurance policy" to show the kidnapping was a hoax.
Aiden Pleterski denies his kidnapping was a hoax on cross-examination at trial for alleged captors
Defence says secret audio captures 'Crypto King' planning his own kidnapping
In the recording — played for the jury on Friday — Pleterski discusses the value of luxury watches, gold bars and cars he says his former landlord, Sandeep Gupta, is hiding for him.
"This is the plan and a roadmap of how this kidnapping is going to play out," defence lawyer Leora Shemesh told Pleterski on cross-examination in Ontario Superior Court in Toronto.
"You are directing these men how you're going to do it and how you're going to sell it.”

Pleterski denied that. Instead, the 28-year-old testified that the recording was made after he was kidnapped and that he lied about Gupta hiding assets in order to sell the need for an in-person meeting with Gupta to his alleged kidnappers, where he hoped to escape.

items: 'Crypto King' faked kidnapping, created video for sympathy, defence says
Secretly recorded videos of 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski meeting alleged kidnapper played at trial

blocks.text: "I know it was taken before the confession video and it was taken after the initial beating," said Pleterski.
Shemesh is representing Alfredo Paladino who is on trial — along with Akil Heywood and Rakeem Henry — for allegedly kidnapping and extorting Pleterski in early December 2022.

From left, Alfredo Paladino, Akil Heywood and Rakeem Henry are accused of kidnapping and extorting the so-called 'Crypto King' Aiden Pleterski in December 2022. (Evan Mitsui/CBC, atlanticmastoronto/Instagram)
Pleterski previously testified that he was beaten, tortured and thought he was going to die during the three-day ordeal.

Shemesh previously called the kidnapping a "farce" Thursday, as she started her cross-examination, alleging Pleterski created a video pretending to be kidnapped in order to gain sympathy from his investors. He also denied both those assertions.

Pleterski was convicted of fraud last month in connection with more than $30 million he took from investors to trade on their behalf. Instead, he spent much of it on his lifestyle. He has yet to be sentenced.

blocks.text: The Crown is alleging Heywood lost a significant amount of money investing with Pleterski and was the "driving force" behind the kidnapping, while Paladino and Henry carried it out. Paladino and Henry are also charged with firearm and assault offences.
All three men have pleaded not guilty.
Beating or fighting?
On Friday, Shemesh also offered an alternative explanation for Pleterski's injuries.

She suggested they were the result of a fight he lost with "Slime," another alleged kidnapper — who is not part of this trial. The defence lawyer said "Slime" was upset because the plan to extract money from Gupta wasn't working and that police were involved.
"No one counted on Gupta calling 911, not even you," said Shemesh to Pleterski.
Again, Pleterski denied that and reiterated that he was kidnapped and beaten by his alleged captors.
Aiden Pleterski testified police took these photos of his injuries after his alleged kidnapping in early December 2022. (Ontario Superior Court)

Pleterski was previously shown photos of his injuries by the Crown and described how he received cuts, burns and bruises from multiple beatings, torture with cigarette burns and cuts with knives during his kidnapping.
However, when asked by Shemesh if he went to the hospital for treatment of these injuries, Pleterski confirmed that he did not.

blocks.text: Shemesh completed her cross-examination on Friday.
Pleterski was testifying all week, and is expected to be back in the witness box on Monday morning for his third cross-examination, this time from Henry's lawyer.
